thread:
ops-bot: INCIDENT PAGE P1 - serving runtime crashloops (us-west-2-prod). Alert: >50% pods in trt-pool-3 restarting. Possible segfaults during model load. Pager: @sre-oncall

sre-oncall: taking pager. tagging runtime & infra.

maya: I'm seeing repeated OOM-ish logs followed by SIGSEGV when model loads start (~step 1 of init). repro on 3 different nodes (gpu-node-12/14/19). Logs attached below.

eng-runner: kubectl -n serving logs trt-runtime-abcde -c runtime --previous
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:01Z] runtime: loading model trt-llm-v2
[2026-03-15T09:12:02Z] allocating device memory: 24.0GB
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] F A I L: segfault at 0 ip 0x7fe9c1a2d1 bf sp 0x7ffeefbff2c0 error 4 in runtime_engine.so[7fe9c1800000+2a0000]
---process exited with signal SIGSEGV (core dumped)---
```

maya: note the libc address in the crash, but the binary is runtime_engine.so (TensorRT fused kernels). stacktrace is noisy, grabbed a short bt from gdb on a core:
```
#0  0x00007fe9c1a2d1bf in memcpy () from /lib64/libc.so.6
#1  0x00007fe9d1e2b4f in trt::plugin::FusedKernel::execute+0x2f (runtime_engine.so)
#2  0x00007fe9d1e3c88 in trt::Engine::run+0x118
#3  0x0000555556a2b0 in load_model (main.cpp:412)
#4  0x0000555556a3f4 in init_process (main.cpp:178)
```

linus: did we roll any driver/kernel updates in the last day? memcpy sigsegv often points to bad GPU pointer or bad driver.

david: yes we rolled nvidia-driver 550.87 -> 554.45 via node image cookbook yesterday at 03:10 UTC for security patch. Only scheduled for non-prod but a cross-region sync happened and hit a few prod nodes.

maya: hmm i can reproduce locally on one node after forcing same driver. but the crash shows runtime_engine.so calling memcpy on a GPU buffer -> likely host memcpy from device-mapped ptr. Could be fused kernel returning a bad pointer on some paths.

eng-runner: quick check: kubectl get pods -n serving -l pool=trt-pool-3 -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount}'
output: 12 11 14 0 2

sre-oncall: customer impact assessment: early telemetry shows 18% failed requests for tenants using trt-pool-3 over last 10m. Affected tenants: alpha-search, chat-proto (subset), internal-evals. Not global yet but trending up.

maya: I'm going to attempt a rollback of the runtime image on one canary pod to the previous build (runtime:2026-03-10) and see if it avoids the segfault. If it clears, we can isolate to runtime changes. If not, likely infra (driver).

ops-bot: deploy-bot started rollout: runtime-deploy -> image runtime:2026-03-10 -> canary trt-pool-3/slot-1

eng-runner: canary pod now up. logs:
```
[2026-03-15T09:22:47Z] runtime: loading model trt-llm-v2
[2026-03-15T09:22:48Z] allocating device memory: 24.0GB
[2026-03-15T09:22:49Z] model loaded successfully, serving
```

maya: canary is stable so far (5 minutes, no crashes). Good signal.

david: that suggests the runtime build change is the trigger. There was a fused-kernel change merged two days ago to optimize prefix copy. cc @linus for kernel review.

linus: I'll revert the fused-kernel change in a branch and request a hotfix build. Meanwhile we need to remediate prod to reduce customer impact: options: 1) rollback runtime image globally; 2) cordon/drain affected nodes (if infra suspected); 3) route traffic away from trt-pool-3 to trt-pool-1/2 if capacity allows. Thoughts?

sre-oncall: prefer to rollback runtime image cluster-wide to known-good (since canary is clean) and then trigger a staged rollout after hotfix. Routing is possible but adds complexity for tenants. I'll do a cluster rollback unless objections.

maya: +1 rollback. we should also collect cores and upload to debug bucket for postmortem.

sre-oncall: executing rollback now. deploy-bot triggered: runtime-deploy -> image runtime:2026-03-10 -> 100%

ops-bot: Rollout started. 56 pods updating across trt pools.

eng-runner: monitoring restarts... crash rate dropping: failed requests down from 18% -> 4% in 3 minutes.

sre-oncall: node-level actions: cordoned gpu-node-12 and drained pods on gpu-node-19 as precaution.
commands run:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-19 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

output: node/gpu-node-19 cordoned and drained.

maya: fetching core dumps: we found core.* in /var/crash on drained nodes, uploading to s3://redwood-debug/1951234567/cores. gdb batch script attached.

eng-runner: CI/build: creating hotfix image with fused-kernel revert: runtime:2026-03-15-hotfix-1. Build passed smoke tests (local TRT emu).

david: once hotfix image ready, we will roll replace runtime:2026-03-10 with hotfix and run canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot created hotfix rollout ticket #DL-4291.

sre-oncall: current status: rollback to runtime:2026-03-10 completed. Slice-level error rate back to baseline (0.8% failed). No new crashloops reported in trt-pool-3. Customer impact contained.

maya: action items: 1) eng: bisect fused-kernel PR and revert upstream + add null-pointer guard in kernel host wrapper (maya/david) 2) infra: verify driver rollout gating to avoid cross-region prod drift (linus/sre) 3) ops: add automated detection for repeated memcpy SIGSEGV pattern to page runtime-oncall earlier (sre-oncall/eng).

david: timeline note: root cause likely bad interaction between fused-kernel change and specific device pointer lifecycle; further investigation on core dumps needed.

linus: I'll follow up with a kernel-level unit test that simulates pinned/mapped buffers and edge-copy paths.

sre-oncall: postmortem owners: maya (lead), linus (infra), david (runtime), follow-up ETA 72h. I will send an incident summary to #postmortems and tag affected customer success teams.

maya: uploading debug artifacts and initial bisect notes to the incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incidents/1951234567

eng-runner: final check: all trt pools stable for 12 minutes, restart counts trending to normal. closing pager but keeping follow-up channel open. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: resolved -> rollback to runtime:2026-03-10. Severity: P1 -> mitigated.

sre-oncall: handoff to oncall follow-up. If crash spikes again, page SRE primary.

maya: thanks team. will post root-cause analysis once bisect completes. :pray:
